claimsToVerify: Field plate armor typically weighed roughly 45 to 55 pounds (20-25 kg), allowing full mobility including running, jumping, and mounting a horse without assistance.
The crane hoisting myth originated largely from Victorian theater staging and Mark Twain's fiction, not medieval reality.
Knights functioned primarily as landowners and estate managers when not engaged in seasonal military campaigns or tournaments.
